title.narrative: School of Olof Palme in Western Sahara

description.narrative: The project is implemented in Western Sahara. The main outcome areas it contributes to are countering the threats to democracy and human rights and opposing the backlash to increase gender equality. The main right holders are women and men in the refugee camps Aousserd, Dakhla, Laayoune and Smara. Through capacity building activities in gender equality and women's rights, education in media, communication, computer, science and administration the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between The Olof Palme Foundation of Western Sahara, Social Democratic Women (district Dalarna and Stockholm) and the Palme Center. The Olof Palme Foundation of Western Sahara The Olof Palme Foundation was founded in 1989 by the Swedish Social Democratic Women. The Foundation has developed from a school that focus on practical education for women to a Foundation that works to empower and mobilise women. The Foundation strives to increase women's participation in the Saharawi society, create opportunities for women to participate in political decision-making processes, as well as encourage women to participate in the development of the local civil society. Social Democratic Women (district Dalarna and Stockholm) S-kvinnor works actively, through both national and international actions to achieve gender equality and solidarity on an international level. Internationally S-kvinnor is working primarily to strengthen women's positions economically, politically and socially, and act against violence against women, trafficking and sexual exploitation.Other Donors to the OrganisationN/AProject ObjectiveProject objectives: - Empower women and support their ability to control their own lives. - Support the development of an organized and efficient women's movement to enhance women's social, economic and political rights. - Women and men have increased their knowledge in gender, equality and women's rights.Actor groupsActors working in cooperation: Local CSOs, regional organisations, international organisations e.g. the UN Relief and Work Agency for Refugees, international media and European organisations e.g. the Union of Swedish Social Democrats. Rights holders: Women, men and youth in the different camps and members of local CSOs.
